sections_in_order: Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews
criteria_location: There are no clinical criteria in the document. Coverage Rationale (p.1-2) delegates to two InterQual products. Only measurable rules in the text are in Applicable Codes > Coding Clarifications (sclerotherapy session limit, once-per-extremity coding) and Definitions (varicose vein >= 3 mm, reflux times). Cosmetic exclusions are in Benefit Considerations. Pages 6-16 are evidence, FDA, references.
procedures_covered: Endovenous ablation of lower extremity superficial truncal or perforator veins (thermal and nonthermal)
Ligation and division with or without stripping or excision
Sclerotherapy of superficial veins (liquid, foam, ultrasound-guided, microfoam)
Unproven: endovenous MOCA, endovenous foam sclerotherapy ablation of incompetent perforators, ablation of recurrent or residual perforator after prior procedure, VenoValve porcine bioprosthetic valve

logic.top_level: other: delegation. Coverage is decided by an external InterQual subset (ablation, ligation) and by a simple code-count rule (sclerotherapy)
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Benefit Considerations bullet list of exclusions: congenital anomaly correction without function, 'Any procedure that does not meet the criteria in the Coverage Rationale section', spider veins/telangiectasias, endovenous ablation of reticular or telangiectatic veins, cosmetic sclerotherapy. Unproven list in Coverage Rationale.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Sclerotherapy only: 'CPT codes 36470 and 36471 are covered for Sclerotherapy (nontruncal, nontelangiectasia) up to three sessions per leg within a year.' Session = one date of service; year = rolling 12 months (365 days). Also: 'Endovenous Ablation of recurrent or residual perforator vein following a prior vein procedure' is unproven.

extraction_hazards: No clinical criteria are extractable; a criteria extractor must return 'delegated' rather than invent leaves.
Table of contents with dot leaders and a right-hand 'Related Policies' column interleaves with the body on page 1.
Definitions contain thresholds that look like criteria (>= 3 mm, 0.5 s) but are not required by any statement.
The 'See Benefit Considerations' note floats at the right margin; sclerotherapy bullets refer to other sections by name only.
Policy History describes a change ('Removed language indicating MOCA of Varicose Veins is unproven') that conflicts with the Coverage Rationale, which still lists MOCA as unproven.
CPT table has no coverage status column; status is only in surrounding prose.
Repeating header/footer ('Proprietary Information of UnitedHealthcare') on every page.
Over 9 pages of clinical evidence and references with study statistics that look like thresholds.
interesting_structures: Pure delegation: a policy whose coverage rationale is a hyperlink to InterQual.
Benefit-language rules (cosmetic exclusions, session caps) live in the policy while clinical criteria live in a vendor product.
Count rule defined in code-specific, session-specific, rolling-window terms (3 sessions per leg per rolling 12 months).
Unproven list for newer technology (MOCA, VenoValve, foam ablation of perforators, recurrent perforator ablation).
Same policy 'may also be applied to Medicare Advantage plans in certain instances' (Instructions for Use).

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: There is nothing to compile: the clinical criteria are in InterQual outside the document. What can be checked is a code gate (unproven/cosmetic codes) and a three-per-rolling-year sclerotherapy rule. A tree built from this file alone would be nearly empty; a checker would need the InterQual subset or must route to a human.
